messages:
Rafael Mendes: We need to settle the lightweight approval path for external comms. Right now status updates get stuck in “who says ok?” esp on Sev1+.

Rafael Mendes: Proposal: default approver = SRE Lead oncall. IC can publish but must @mention SRE lead before publish. Security only for specific triggers.

Sean Gallagher: +1 to having a default. But we need to be super explicit on when Security/Legal gets pulled in. Otherwise folks either over-escalate or skip.

Tomáš Novák: Oncall perspective: if approval requires paging Security at 3am we’ll either miss cadence or we’ll go rogue. Need a “safe-by-default” template where approval is implicit unless we deviate.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Agree. We can define “pre-approved language” (templates) that doesn’t require Security review in the moment. Security review required if the update includes (a) suspected malicious activity, (b) data exposure possibility, (c) auth/session compromise, (d) vulnerability/exploit speculation, (e) law enforcement request.

Marcus Lin: + add “provider incident with contractual constraints” bucket. We can say “upstream provider networking issue” but not name the vendor/region details sometimes.

Dev Patel: From Support: biggest pain is long periods w/ no updates because we’re waiting on approval. Even “we’re investigating, next update in 30m” helps.

Rafael Mendes: OK, so approval model:
1) Status update using templates (Investigating/Identified/Monitoring/Resolved) => SRE Lead OR IC can publish w/o extra approval.
2) Deviations (mentions security, data, vendor, customer-specific) => must get Security + (maybe Legal) signoff.

Sean Gallagher: I’d tweak: IC can always publish the first update immediately (investigating), but should notify SRE Lead in-thread. Subsequent updates follow normal flow.

Tomáš Novák: +1. First update is time critical and should be template-only.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Works. If the first update includes anything beyond template (e.g., “unauthorized access”), then Security should be looped immediately even if we still publish.

Michael Grant: For Legal/privacy: avoid customer identifiers + avoid stating/guessing breach impact. Use “we are investigating reports of…” and “no evidence at this time…” only if we’ve checked. If there’s any plausible privacy impact, loop me or Olga.

Rafael Mendes: Can we define the actual “approvers” list so oncall knows who to ping?

Dr. Aisha Rahman: For Security: oncall = @sec-oncall (me/Marcus rotation). If it’s not Sev0/S1 and you just need a quick wording check, drop in #eng-security with the draft.

Marcus Lin: Also please don’t post stack traces / request IDs / IPs to public status, even redacted. Seen that happen once.

Sean Gallagher: Decision framing:
- Default: IC or SRE Lead can publish status page updates using the approved templates.
- If outside templates OR any disclosure trigger => Security review required before publish (unless time-critical; then publish minimal template + state “Security engaged”).
- Post-incident summaries: require SRE Lead review + Security async review before publishing for Sev0/S1; for Sev2+ SRE Lead only unless triggers.

Dev Patel: Love it. Also can we add a step: Support gets a heads up in #support-incidents when it’s Sev1+? Even a link to status update draft.

Rafael Mendes: Yep, comms side channel is fine. That’s separate from “approval” though.

Tomáš Novák: Where do we document this? We’ll need it in the runbook + the policy page.

Rafael Mendes: I’ll add to external-comms-approval-policy Confluence page draft. Talia can you sanity-check wording aligns with the broader status transparency work?

Talia Benson: Yep. Please include a simple decision tree and the “pre-approved template language” concept. That’ll unblock the incident-bot prompts too.

Sean Gallagher: Action items:
- Rafael: update policy doc w/ decision tree + approver roles.
- Aisha/Marcus: provide final trigger list + example safe phrasing (provider incident, suspected security, etc.).
- Tomáš: update runbook section “When to get approval”.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: I’ll drop trigger list + example phrases by EOD. :thumbsup:

Marcus Lin: +1. Also include “don’t mention CVE / exploit chain / bypass details” as a hard rule.

Rafael Mendes: Great. I’ll post the draft link in-thread once it’s up for comments.
